sourceDateMeaning: Official pages were accessed and reviewed on this date; vendor page publication dates were not consistently exposed.

claims.sourceExcerpt: Connect GitHub repositories to v0 and ship changes through branches, previews, pull requests, and CI.
claims.scope: Current public v0-to-GitHub workflow when a project is connected to a repository; account roles and repository permissions apply.
claims.value: Connected chats use a base branch and isolated working branches; v0 pushes generated changes to the working branch and supports pull-request review before merge. The connected GitHub repository is the code source of truth.
claims.limitation: This establishes the documented Git workflow, not transfer of Vercel project settings, secrets, databases, domains, or a tested export of every project asset.

claims.scope: Documented preview and production deployment path for v0 projects.
claims.value: v0 deploys projects to Vercel; working branches can receive preview deployments, and publishing updates the linked Vercel project's production deployment and URL.
claims.limitation: A Vercel deployment path is not evidence that an app can be deployed unchanged to another host; portability was not tested.

claims.evidenceNote: Official page opened, but no short passage directly supporting the portability boundary was located in this review.
claims.scope: Publicly documented database integrations and data export or migration behavior for a v0-created project.
claims.value: The docs describe connecting providers including Upstash, Neon, Supabase, and Vercel Blob, and selecting existing stores.
claims.limitation: The reviewed page does not establish a complete data export, schema migration, credential transfer, backup/restore, or provider-exit procedure for a project. Do not infer either portability or lock-in from this gap.

claims.sourceExcerpt: Add real functionality to your application by integrating with databases, APIs, and external services.
claims.excerptLocator: Quickstart, Integrate: Connect external services, line 143
claims.scope: Examples and integration paths documented by v0; availability depends on the connected provider and project configuration.
claims.value: Official docs describe database and AI integrations, external APIs using project environment variables, and a Stripe payment integration; documented database examples include Neon, Supabase, Upstash, and Vercel Blob.
claims.limitation: This is not an exhaustive compatibility list and does not establish plan-independent access, successful integration for every app, or transferability of provider accounts and credentials.

claims.excerptLocator: Plans and Pricing, Free plan, line 14
claims.scope: Public v0 plan and model-usage listing as displayed on the review date; excludes individualized checkout and connected Vercel service usage.
claims.value: The public page listed Free at $0 with a seven-message daily limit, Plus at a displayed $30 per user/month with included credits, Business at $100 per user/month, and custom Enterprise terms; model token rates are usage-specific.
claims.limitation: Displayed prices, promotions, included credits, tax, eligibility, and account entitlements can change or vary. The reviewed page does not establish total Vercel hosting, database, or third-party provider cost for a built app; confirm current account checkout and provider billing before estimating total cost.

claims.sourceExcerpt: required human reviews must be completed in GitHub.
claims.scope: Public evidence about GitHub and Vercel permissions in the documented development and publishing workflow; not a complete operations responsibility matrix.
claims.value: Publishing and deployment actions depend on v0, GitHub repository, and Vercel project roles; branch protections and required human reviews can block publishing.
claims.limitation: The reviewed docs do not define the customer's ongoing responsibility for application security, incident response, backups, upgrades, monitoring, or service-level operations. Do not claim those duties are automated or contractually assigned based on this page.

claims.evidenceNote: Official page opened, but no short passage directly supporting the complete handoff Claim was located in this review.
claims.scope: Documented Git and GitHub source control inside Replit; does not cover every generated or hosted resource.
claims.value: Replit documents Git-backed version control, GitHub connectivity, importing, modifying and pushing code between Replit and GitHub, branch workflows, and Git CLI access.
claims.limitation: Code synchronization does not prove that database contents, secrets, domains, deployment configuration, integrations, or account-level resources move with the repository.

claims.sourceExcerpt: Autoscale is the default and recommended choice
claims.scope: Publicly documented Replit deployment modes and their broad operating models.
claims.value: Replit documents Autoscale, Static, Reserved VM, and Scheduled deployments with different runtime and billing models; deployment configuration and resource selection are project-specific.
claims.limitation: This establishes available Replit deployment choices, not portability of a deployed application to another host or equivalence of runtime behavior there.

claims.sourceExcerpt: Your published app needs its own production database.
claims.scope: Documented database data export/import workflow; does not cover every app resource or automated whole-project migration.
claims.value: Replit documents exporting database data to a file and, for a specific shared-database migration scenario, using PostgreSQL dump/restore commands to move data between development and production databases.
claims.limitation: The procedure is scenario-specific and may require maintenance planning; custom roles or policies may need additional handling. It does not prove turnkey migration of all schemas, integrations, secrets, files, domains, jobs, and deployment settings to another provider.

claims.evidenceNote: Official page opened, but no short passage directly supporting the stated integration scope was located in this review.
claims.scope: Integration classes documented for Replit Agent; exact features depend on plan, connector, permissions, and supplied credentials.
claims.value: Replit distinguishes managed integrations, first-party Connectors, external integrations requiring user-provided API keys, and paid third-party Agent services; most Connectors require paid plans, while some are available on Free and Replit-managed integrations are available to Free plan builders.
claims.limitation: Availability, account authorization, scopes, plan eligibility, and provider charges differ by integration. The categories do not establish that every integration is supported on every plan or portable to another development platform.

claims.evidenceNote: Official page opened, but no short passage directly supporting the complete effort-based pricing Claim was located in this review.
claims.scope: Public AI and cloud usage billing model; exact plan price, credits, workload consumption, and checkout are account- and usage-dependent.
claims.value: Official docs describe effort-based paid Agent usage, third-party Agent services charged at provider API rates, and credits applying across Agent and Replit cloud services such as published apps, storage, and databases.
claims.limitation: A subscription price is not a total application cost. Actual spend varies with request complexity, selected model or provider, plan allowance, and current account terms; this page does not establish one universal build or monthly operating cost.
